title: First Project in UE5 with Claude Ultra
author: 999Jupiter999
selftext:
I just want to preface this post by saying I have created a few other projects before with Claude and with other AI agents as well but this was my first time doing a project at all in Unreal Engine 5.

Simply put, the game is obviously a horror game, sort of inspired by the TV show Supernatural and heavily inspired by real folklore stories in the US.

I am on the **Max Subscription**, I have been working on this project for about 2 weeks. With about 2 months of brainstorming and planning before ever starting it, I thought it was just way too big to build but here we are. I am doing it completely solo with just this Max account + Tripo for some of the models. Total Cost in API so far is about $4900, obviously I haven't paid that out of pocket.

There are still of course many glitches and things that need perfecting, but the goal is to have a playable first mission (Wendigo) by January '27. Eventually if we get to a full release, the game is planned to be a Solo OR a Dup experience. **Track & Hunt "Cryptid and Supernatural Entities" in C.A.S.E , for PC.**

Please let me know your thoughts/questions if any, would you or a friend play this?

comments.author: DraconicBlade
comments.body:
Your opener has the same tree model right next to itself center frame in scene 2, also repeating tree models right frame.

Immediately writing it off. Reusing assets in the same shot in under ten seconds. You have told me im being sold leftover casserole breakfast lunch and dinner.

replies.author: imlo2
replies.body:
You do realize that most games re-use tree assets etc. very heavily. Very rarely is real dynamic generation used in any games. They are just instanced with rotation and scaling, and there might not often be more than a handful of variants of one tree type or a rock or such. Otherwise you lose easily benefits of instanced drawing, batching etc. This applies to all the big AAA games etc. What is unfortunate if anything that two trees in same rotation and scale are seen side by side.   
  
But I wouldn't start to call the project being something like leftover food because of that. Would you say that face to face in a review session at a game studio?

replies.author: DraconicBlade
replies.body:
I do realize that. When its slammed in my face immediately, I also realize there's oversight. Lack of care, inattention to detail.

So, I'm gonna assume that note carries through the entire piece.
